KEY 3 — the geometric occupancy split in _m_axis_occupancy_cap (triton.py ~818: per_axis = int(budget ** (1.0/n_tunable_m))). Distributes the collapse budget across n tunable m-axes by the n-th root. 261	    """Seed all-ones ``block_sizes`` for split/join rotate kernels (rope).

274	        if env.config_spec.matmul_facts:

304	class TritonPointwiseSeedHeuristic(AutotunerHeuristic):
305	    """Seed a bandwidth-saturating tile for PURE elementwise/pointwise kernels.
306	
307	    A pointwise kernel reads its inputs, computes, and writes its outputs with no
308	    reduction / matmul / loop-carried accumulator — it is BANDWIDTH-bound. The compiler
309	    default tiles it at ``block_size=32`` (``BlockSizeSpec._fragment``: ``total_ndim <= 2
310	    and reduction_numel <= 128``), moving only ~10% of HBM (~5-7x slower than a saturating
311	    tile; measured headroom in ``_lab/pointwise``). This seed sizes the tile to (a) a byte
312	    budget that saturates HBM and (b) the grid occupancy (size_hint-aware), keyed on the
313	    derived ``PointwiseElementwiseFact`` (bytes/elem + total numel) — NEVER on the
314	    activation identity or a dtype literal. Fires on the presence of that fact, which is
315	    built only on the ABSENCE of the reduction/matmul/accumulator facts (disjointness rule),
316	    so it never claws a reducing kernel into the pointwise track.
317	    """
318	
319	    name = "triton_pointwise"
320	    backend = "triton"
321	
322	    # Hill-climbed constants (see _lab/pointwise/NOTEBOOK.md). TILE_BYTES=8192 gives a ~1024-elem
323	    # tile for traffic-3 (swiglu/geglu/residual_add) and ~2048 for traffic-2 (relu²/bias_gelu) —
324	    # the robust zone: 1-D kernels are flat across 1-8K, but N-D/traffic-2 kernels (bias_gelu) lose
325	    # ~5-25% at 4096 vs 2048, so the smaller budget lifts the worst kernel with no 1-D regression.
326	    TILE_BYTES = 8192  # target HBM bytes moved per tile
327	    MIN_WAVES = 8  # grid >= num_sm * MIN_WAVES (size_hint-aware grid floor)
328	    BLOCK_FLOOR = 256  # never regress toward the bs=32 default

332	        return bool(env.config_spec.pointwise_facts)

334	    @classmethod
335	    def get_seed_config(cls, env: CompileEnvironment, device_ir: DeviceIR) -> Config:
336	        from ...runtime import get_num_sm
337	        from ...runtime.config import Config as _Config
338	
339	        spec = env.config_spec
340	        fact = spec.pointwise_facts[0]
341	        num_sm = max(1, get_num_sm(env.device))
342	        bytes_per_elem = max(1, fact.bytes_per_elem)
343	        # PINNED per-program elements: a grid-pinned (block_size=1) or specialized full-extent
344	        # axis contributes elements to EVERY program but has no tunable tile, so the distributor
345	        # (which only sees spec.block_sizes) cannot account for them. Their product is the work
346	        # each program already does; the tunable dims only need to fill the REMAINING budget.
347	        # (A grid-pinned block_size=1 axis contributes 1 -> no effect; a specialized group_size
348	        # contributes its full width.) Read the fixed block size from env.block_sizes (keyed by
349	        # ALL ids) via an empty Config, NOT size_hint (which is the whole-axis extent, not the
350	        # per-program tile).
351	        tunable = set(spec.block_sizes.valid_block_ids())
352	        pinned_elems = 1
353	        for info in env.block_sizes:
354	            if info.block_id in tunable:
355	                continue
356	            value = info.from_config(_Config(block_sizes=[]))
357	            if isinstance(value, (int, torch.SymInt)):
358	                pinned_elems *= max(1, int(value))
359	        # Bytes-aware target tile (in elements), DISCOUNTED by the pinned per-program work: a
360	        # traffic-3 kernel moves 50% more bytes per element than traffic-2, so for the same byte
361	        # budget it gets a SMALLER element tile.
362	        target = max(1, (cls.TILE_BYTES // bytes_per_elem) // pinned_elems)
363	        # size_hint-aware: cap the tile so the grid keeps the SMs busy on small problems (the
364	        # occupancy cap already uses the pinned-inclusive total_numel, so divide it too).
365	        max_tile = max(1, fact.total_numel // (num_sm * cls.MIN_WAVES) // pinned_elems)
366	        target = max(1, min(target, max_tile))
367	        # Floor (the never-regress-to-bs=32 guard) likewise discounts the pinned work: a program
368	        # already covering >= BLOCK_FLOOR elements via pinned axes needs no tunable floor.
369	        floor = max(1, cls.BLOCK_FLOOR // pinned_elems)
370	        target = max(floor, target)
371	        # block_sizes is the only non-default field; num_warps/num_stages/pid_type stay at the
372	        # compiler defaults (4 / 1 / 'flat'), so emitting them would be inert (Gate F). A measured
373	        # num_warps ramp for large tiles is a BROADEN-queue item.
374	        return Config(block_sizes=cls._seed_block_sizes(spec, target, floor))
375	
376	    @staticmethod
377	    def _pow2_floor(value: int) -> int:
378	        return 1 << (value.bit_length() - 1) if value >= 1 else 1
379	
380	    @classmethod
381	    def _clamp_dim(cls, target: int, bs_spec: BlockSizeSpec, floor: int) -> int:
382	        # Round DOWN to a pow2 within [floor (and the spec's correctness min), max_size]. max_size
383	        # is next_pow2(extent), so capping there (rather than pre-capping at the raw size_hint) lets
384	        # the inner tile COVER a short row in one masked tile (extent 768 -> 1024, not floored to
385	        # 512). autotuner_min is the AUTOTUNER's search floor, NOT a seed constraint (the reduction
386	        # and split-join seeds emit block=1 below it), so it is intentionally not applied here.
387	        cand = cls._pow2_floor(max(1, target))
388	        cand = max(cand, floor, bs_spec.min_size)
389	        cand = min(cand, bs_spec.max_size)
390	        return max(1, cand)
391	
392	    @classmethod
393	    def _seed_block_sizes(
394	        cls, spec: ConfigSpec, target: int, floor: int | None = None
395	    ) -> list[int]:
396	        """Distribute the target tile (in elements) across the block dims, INNERMOST first,
397	        SPILLING the leftover budget outward. The innermost (contiguous, last) dim takes as much
398	        of the budget as its extent allows (capped at max_size = next_pow2(extent), so a short row
399	        is covered in one masked tile); whatever budget it cannot absorb spills to the next-outer
400	        dim, and so on. Because a row-major tensor stores rows contiguously, an ``[R, N]`` tile of
401	        a short-N tensor is still a coalesced ``R*N`` contiguous block — so a tall-skinny tensor
402	        (small inner extent, e.g. image RGBA N=4 or a per-head N=64) gets a budget-sized tile (e.g.
403	        ``[128, 8]``) instead of a starved ``[1, 8]`` that regresses below the bs=32 default. For a
404	        WIDE row (extent >= budget) the inner absorbs the whole budget and the outer dims stay 1
405	        (``[1, 1024]``) — the 1-D-flatten-equivalent coalesced run; for a 1-D kernel this is just
406	        ``[clamp(target)]``."""
407	        inner_floor = cls.BLOCK_FLOOR if floor is None else floor
408	        n = len(spec.block_sizes)
409	        specs = [cast("BlockSizeSpec", spec.block_sizes[i]) for i in range(n)]
410	        block = [1] * n
411	        remaining = max(1, target)
412	        for i in reversed(
413	            range(n)
414	        ):  # innermost (contiguous) dim first, spill the rest outward
415	            dim_floor = inner_floor if i == n - 1 else 1
416	            block[i] = cls._clamp_dim(remaining, specs[i], dim_floor)
417	            remaining = max(1, remaining // block[i])
418	            if remaining <= 1:
419	                break
420	        return block

423	def _triton_reduction_eligible(env: CompileEnvironment, device_ir: DeviceIR) -> bool:
424	    """Gate: at least one ``ReductionFact`` and no ``matmul_facts``. Admits both tracks
425	    (standard rollable, user-tiled); excludes GEMMs.
426	
427	    FIRES on a MULTI-FACT kernel too (two genuinely-independent reductions in separate loops,
428	    e.g. ``out1 = x.sum(-1); out2 = y.sum(-1)`` -> two ``ReductionFact``s). The old ``== 1`` gate
429	    declined those into the (bad) upstream default -- an under-firing FENCE narrowing to the
430	    single-reduction curriculum (no corpus kernel has >1 fact). A seed is never forced (a worse
431	    seed only costs autotuning time, never correctness), so FIRING a best-guess on the dominant
432	    (max-extent) reduction beats declining into the default (method §2 'prefer to fire'); the
433	    seeded loop is sized correctly and the other loop's tiles ride the generic per-axis path.
434	    ``_reduction_primary_fact`` picks the dominant fact for the seed."""
435	    spec = env.config_spec
436	    return len(spec.reduction_facts) >= 1 and not spec.matmul_facts

439	def _reduction_primary_fact(spec: ConfigSpec) -> ReductionFact:
440	    """The fact the seed sizes when a kernel has MORE THAN ONE ReductionFact (independent
441	    reductions in separate loops): the DOMINANT one by reduction extent (``size_hint``), the
442	    same max-extent tie-break the single-fact dominant-axis pick uses. The single-fact case
443	    returns ``reduction_facts[0]`` unchanged (byte-identical). A worse pick only costs autotune
444	    time (the other loop's tiles are still sized by ``_build_block_sizes``); the dominant
445	    reduction is the one whose mis-size would hurt most, so seed it."""
446	    facts = spec.reduction_facts
447	    return max(facts, key=lambda f: f.size_hint)

451	    """standard vs user-tiled discriminator: standard iff the rdim is NOT a ``block_sizes``
452	    entry. Covers a roller-rolled rdim (a ``reduction_loops`` entry) AND a MATERIALIZED rdim
453	    (an inner ``reduction=True`` axis the roller declined to roll, in NEITHER spec --
454	    rms/ln/instance backward); user-tiled is the rdim-is-a-block_sizes case.

459	def _grid_rows(env: CompileEnvironment, m_block_ids: tuple[int, ...]) -> int:
460	    """Product of the static M-axis (non-reduction grid) extents — the program count the
461	    reduction launches, the numerator of the occupancy ``grid_rows // num_sm``. Returns 0
462	    if any extent is not a statically-resolvable size (a dynamic grid has no compile-time
463	    occupancy, so the occupancy-gated narrow-w1 lever declines).
464	    """
465	    grid_rows = 1
466	    for mbid in m_block_ids:
467	        size = env.block_sizes[mbid].size
468	        if not isinstance(size, (int, torch.SymInt)):
469	            return 0
470	        grid_rows *= env.size_hint(size)
471	    return grid_rows

474	class _TritonReductionSeedBase(AutotunerHeuristic):
475	    """Shared base for the two Triton inner-reduction seed heuristics. Both share the
476	    workload facts (``ReductionFact``), the M_BLOCK-aware reduction-block lever
477	    (``_reduction_rblock``, from which each track derives ``persistent``), the ``num_warps``
478	    ramp, eviction provenance, and the block-size builders; the subclasses differ only in
479	    mapping that decision onto knobs:
480	
481	    - **standard** (:class:`TritonStandardReductionHeuristic`): Helion rolls the rdim into
482	      a ``reduction_loops`` loop.
483	    - **user-tiled** (:class:`TritonUserTiledReductionHeuristic`): the user hand-writes the
484	      ``hl.tile`` loop, so the reduction axis is a ``block_sizes`` entry (plain user-tiled
485	      softmax, carried-2-D-tile kl_div/jsd, reduce-then-apply welford).
486	
487	    Not registered; only the subclasses are.
488	    """
489	
490	    backend = "triton"
491	    HARDWARE_TARGETS = (("cuda", "sm90"),)
492	
493	    # Occupancy floor for the M-axis widen: keep the post-widen grid >= num_sm * MIN_WAVES so
494	    # collapsing a fan-out sibling never under-occupies the machine (mirrors the pointwise seed's
495	    # MIN_WAVES grid floor).
496	    MIN_WAVES = 8
497	    # Looped-fallback reduction chunk (pow2) for a row that does not fit the persistent
498	    # residency budget. ``_reduction_rblock`` shrinks it when a raised M_BLOCK divides the
499	    # footprint budget below it; at M_BLOCK==1 it is used as-is.
500	    LOOPED_CHUNK = 16384
501	    # Per-program byte budget for LOOP-CARRIED 2-D accumulator tiles ([M_BLOCK, R_BLOCK], e.g.
502	    # kl_div/jsd): caps R_BLOCK via num_carried_2d_tiles. Tightest budget -- resident the whole loop.
503	    CARRIED_TILE_MAX_BYTES = 16384
504	    # Per-program persistent byte ceiling. The resident reduction tile is [M_BLOCK, R_BLOCK]
505	    # in BOTH tracks (the persistent load and the looped accumulator both carry the M_BLOCK
506	    # dim), so the per-program footprint is ``m_block * r_block * itemsize`` and every cap
507	    # below divides the budget by M_BLOCK. Above it a wide resident tile spills register/SMEM,
508	    # so the reduction loops a chunk instead. ~240 KiB, just over H100 SMEM.
509	    ROW_PERSIST_MAX_BYTES = 245760
510	    # (Removed: PERSISTENT_REDUCTION_MAX and FULL_WIDTH_PERSIST_MAX_ELEMS -- both orphaned dead
511	    # constants with no readers. PERSISTENT_REDUCTION_MAX was the co-gate of the deleted
512	    # `reduction_is_pinned` field, dropped when the m-axis widen went footprint-only (Round 5);
513	    # FULL_WIDTH_PERSIST_MAX_ELEMS was the element cap removed from `extent_held` when the byte
514	    # budgets (ROW_PERSIST_MAX_BYTES + LIVE_PERSIST_BUDGET) superseded it. Re-add recipe in the
515	    # removed-heuristics log if a measured spill ever needs an explicit element/extent cap.)
516	    # Max resident bytes a PERSISTENT reduction body (body_live_tiles full-width tiles) may hold
517	    # before catastrophic register spill. Only REMOVES persistence from a heavy body, never grows it.
518	    LIVE_PERSIST_BUDGET = 3 * 245760
519	    # M-COLLAPSE (grad-parameter reduction, e.g. bias_grad): max rows one CTA reduces in a single
520	    # in-register inner tile, capped so the reduction tree + [rows, feature] tile don't spill.
521	    M_COLLAPSE_MAX_CTA = 256
522	    # M-COLLAPSE inner reduction tile byte budget: a grad-parameter collapse is memory-bound, so
523	    # the inner [rows, feature] tile wants the SMALLEST footprint (~2-8 rows) for CTA occupancy.
524	    M_COLLAPSE_TILE_BYTES = 32768
525	    # No welford "structured-combine floor": welford is memory-bound (profiler-confirmed),
526	    # so a wide combine tile only spills — register-residency via the reduction footprint cap
527	    # is what matters. The apply/normalize tile gets the SAME M_BLOCK-aware footprint cap as
528	    # the reduction tile, NOT a flat per-row cap (which needlessly narrowed the memory-bound
529	    # apply pass); applied inline in ``_build_block_sizes``.
530	
531	    # NARROW-row single-warp (occupancy-gated): a narrow reduction extent wants ONE warp (the
532	    # cross-warp reduction tree is pure overhead; w1 reduces in-register via shuffle). The win
533	    # inverts past an occupancy ceiling (the SMs saturate), so it is gated on a row-byte cap
534	    # AND an occupancy cap, both keyed on input_load_itemsize (the HBM-load element width —
535	    # faithful and dtype-agnostic, unlike the fp32-promoted accumulator itemsize which is 4 at
536	    # both dtypes):
537	    #   - row cap: rnumel * input_load_itemsize <= NARROW_W1_MAX_BYTES.
538	    #   - occ cap: occ * row_bytes <= NARROW_W1_OCC_BYTE_LIMIT (a wider row saturates at lower
539	    #     occupancy, so the ceiling is on the product, not a flat occ).
540	    NARROW_W1_MAX_BYTES = 2048
541	    NARROW_W1_OCC_BYTE_LIMIT = 262144
542	
543	    @staticmethod
544	    def _resident_itemsize(fact: ReductionFact) -> int:
545	        """Element width (bytes) of the RESIDENT reduction tile the byte budgets bound. A naked
546	        Helion reduction tree accumulates in fp32 REGARDLESS of the input dtype (only ``var_mean``
547	        differs), so the live ``[M_BLOCK, R_BLOCK]`` tile a residency cap protects is fp32-wide
548	        (>=4 B) even when the INPUT is bf16/fp16 (``fact.itemsize == 2``). Keying the cap on the
549	        raw input itemsize UNDER-COUNTS the resident footprint 2x at half precision -> it would
550	        admit a spilling persistent tile / over-wide M in the band where the fp32 accumulator
551	        exceeds the cap but the bf16-input count does not (saturation-check finding,
552	        ``probes/gen/sat_bf16_reduction.py``). Floor at 4 so the cap bounds the genuine resident
553	        width. (The I/O-bound ``num_warps`` narrow-row lever correctly keeps ``input_load_itemsize``
554	        -- that one IS about HBM load width, not resident accumulator width.) The dtype-faithful
555	        fix: ``max(itemsize, 4)``, applied only to the loop-carried-fp32-accumulator residency caps.
556	        """
557	        return max(4, fact.itemsize)

559	    @classmethod
560	    def _carried_tile_budget(cls, fact: ReductionFact, co_resident: int = 1) -> int:
561	        """The per-program ELEMENT budget (NOT yet pow2-rounded) for ONE axis of a reduction
562	        carrying loop-resident 2-D accumulator tiles (kl_div, jsd): ``CARRIED_TILE_MAX_BYTES``
563	        divided by the accumulator itemsize, the carried-tile count, AND any ``co_resident`` width
564	        co-held in the same ``[axis, co_resident]`` tile. ONE budget expression both carried-tile
565	        consumers share (Defect §5c duplicated-cap-stack collapse); each caller applies its own
566	        pow2 rounding (a tile-size TARGET rounds up; a largest-that-FITS widen rounds down):
567	          - ``co_resident=1`` (``_carried_tile_r_block_cap`` -> ``_reduction_rblock``): the carried
568	            tile is ``[M_BLOCK=1-seed, R_BLOCK]`` and we size R_BLOCK.
569	          - ``co_resident=r_block_resident`` (``_build_block_sizes`` m_block widen): widening M by
570	            ``k`` holds ``[k, R_BLOCK]``, so divide by the resident R_BLOCK.
571	        ``max(1, ..)`` guards a zero itemsize / tile count / co_resident.
572	        """
573	        return cls.CARRIED_TILE_MAX_BYTES // (
574	            cls._resident_itemsize(fact)
575	            * max(1, fact.num_carried_2d_tiles)
576	            * max(1, co_resident)
577	        )

579	    @classmethod
580	    def _carried_tile_r_block_cap(cls, fact: ReductionFact) -> int:
581	        """Pow2 R_BLOCK ceiling for a carried-2D-tile reduction -- the shared
582	        ``_carried_tile_budget`` (co_resident=1) rounded UP to a pow2 tile-size target."""
583	        from ..._utils import next_power_of_2 as _np2
584	
585	        return _np2(max(1, cls._carried_tile_budget(fact)))

587	    @classmethod
588	    def _num_warps(
589	        cls, fact: ReductionFact, num_sm: int = 0, grid_rows: int = 0
590	    ) -> int:
591	        """Scale num_warps with the reduction extent (pow2, per NumWarpsFragment):
592	        rnumel <= 1024 -> 4, <= 4096 -> 8, <= 16384 -> 16, > 16384 -> 32. Too few
593	        under-occupies the SM, too many wastes the reduction tree.
594	
595	        NARROW-row single-warp refinement at the LOW end (the occupancy-gated lever): a
596	        narrow row at low/moderate occupancy wants ONE warp (the cross-warp reduction tree
597	        is pure overhead — see ``NARROW_W1_MAX_BYTES``). Fires only when the row-byte cap AND
598	        the resident-pressure cap (``occ * row_bytes <= NARROW_W1_OCC_BYTE_LIMIT``) hold; both
599	        key on ``input_load_itemsize`` (faithful, no dtype-kind branch) and the occ ceiling
600	        scales DOWN as the row grows (a wider row cliffs at lower occupancy). Needs ``num_sm``
601	        (0 disables it, e.g. an off-device caller). Disjoint from the wide-row branch below
602	        (``NARROW_W1_MAX_BYTES`` << the rnumel>16384 region), so the two never interact.
603	        """
604	        rnumel = fact.size_hint
605	        ils = fact.input_load_itemsize
606	        row_bytes = rnumel * ils
607	        # NARROW-row single-warp (see NARROW_W1_MAX_BYTES); needs a known device + static grid.
608	        have_enough_information = num_sm > 0 and ils > 0 and grid_rows > 0
609	        if have_enough_information:
610	            occ = grid_rows // num_sm
611	            if (
612	                fact.num_carried_2d_tiles
613	                == 0  # not a carried-2-D-tile reduction (kl_div/jsd)
614	                and row_bytes <= cls.NARROW_W1_MAX_BYTES
615	                and occ * row_bytes <= cls.NARROW_W1_OCC_BYTE_LIMIT
616	            ):
617	                return 1
618	        # >16384 (not >=) so a 16384-wide row stays w16, excluding the w32 regression there.
619	        warps32_min_elems = 16384
620	        if rnumel > warps32_min_elems:
621	            return 32
622	        if rnumel <= 1024:
623	            return 4
624	        if rnumel <= 4096:
625	            return 8
626	        return 16

628	    @classmethod
629	    def _block_floor(cls, bs_spec: BlockSizeSpec) -> int:
630	        """The smallest valid block size for an entry, used for every non-reduction axis
631	        the seed does not widen. Prefers one row/program but honors a raised
632	        ``autotuner_min`` (large-M shapes) rather than emitting an invalid ``block_size=1``.
633	        """
634	        return max(1, bs_spec.min_size, bs_spec.autotuner_min)

636	    @classmethod
637	    def _resident_tile_cap(
638	        cls,
639	        spec: ConfigSpec,
640	        fact: ReductionFact,
641	        inner_resident_elems: int = 1,
642	        r_block_resident: int = 1,
643	    ) -> int:
644	        """Max pow2 tile (along one axis) that keeps the resident live set inside the
645	        per-program register budget: ``tile <= ROW_PERSIST_MAX_BYTES /
646	        (M_BLOCK * r_block_resident * inner_resident_elems * itemsize)``.
647	
648	        ``r_block_resident`` is the resident width of the reduction tile co-held with the axis
649	        being capped (default 1). For the M-AXIS widen branch this is the rdim's resident extent
650	        (``next_pow2(size_hint)`` when persistent, else the rolled chunk): widening an m-axis by
651	        ``k`` holds a ``[k, R_BLOCK]`` reduction tile, so the footprint is ``k * R_BLOCK *
652	        itemsize`` and the cap must divide by ``R_BLOCK`` -- WITHOUT it, a wide-reduction kernel
653	        (rms_norm, R_BLOCK=16384) is told it can widen M to thousands of rows (the cap returns
654	        ~32768) and spills catastrophically (~10x), while a tiny-reduction kernel
655	        (per_token_group, R_BLOCK=128) correctly widens its parallel sibling. Dividing by the
656	        resident R_BLOCK is what makes the floor-vs-widen decision fall out of the footprint
657	        arithmetic alone -- no row-vs-sibling axis classification. Default 1 keeps the
658	        apply/normalize-loop caller (a flat ``[M_BLOCK, tile]`` set) byte-identical.
659	
660	        ``inner_resident_elems`` is the PRODUCT of the extents of any OTHER axes that are
661	        co-resident in the same tile alongside the one being capped (default 1). The
662	        apply/normalize-loop caller holds a flat ``[M_BLOCK, tile]`` set, so it passes 1 (the
663	        cap is byte-identical to the prior formula). The independent-loop caller's tile is
664	        ``[M_BLOCK, tile, *pinned_inner]`` (rms_norm_per_block: a ``[1, groups, group_size]``
665	        per-group quant tile), so it passes the pinned inner product (``group_size``) -- without
666	        it the cap under-counts the footprint by that factor and would admit a spilling tile.
667	
668	        CAVEAT (best-estimate, subject to change): ``ROW_PERSIST_MAX_BYTES`` is borrowed from
669	        the persistent-reduction path -- it was tuned as the resident-row budget for a reduction
670	        tree, NOT for an independent map/quant loop, whose register pressure profile differs.
671	        The footprint ACCOUNTING above is faithful (it now counts every co-resident axis), but
672	        the BUDGET CONSTANT itself is a reused estimate, validated only against rms_norm_per_block
673	        (whose real shapes stay well under it, so the cap never actually bites there -- it only
674	        guards a hypothetical wide independent loop). When a real kernel exercises a large
675	        branch-4 loop that this clamps, re-tune the ceiling for the map case rather than assume
676	        the reduction budget transfers; a dedicated constant may be warranted then.
677	        """
678	        from ..._utils import prev_power_of_2
679	
680	        m_block = cls._m_block_product(spec, fact)
681	        denom = (
682	            m_block
683	            * max(1, r_block_resident)
684	            * max(1, inner_resident_elems)
685	            * cls._resident_itemsize(fact)
686	        )
687	        budget = cls.ROW_PERSIST_MAX_BYTES // max(1, denom)
688	        return prev_power_of_2(max(1, budget))

690	    @classmethod
691	    def _pinned_inner_resident_elems(
692	        cls, spec: ConfigSpec, fact: ReductionFact, loop_block_id: int
693	    ) -> int:
694	        """Product of the extents of the PINNED inner axes co-resident with an independent
695	        (branch-4) loop tile -- the factor ``_resident_tile_cap`` must divide the budget by so
696	        the ``[M_BLOCK, loop_tile, *pinned_inner]`` footprint is bounded faithfully.
697	
698	        A pinned inner axis is one that is NOT tunable (absent from
699	        ``block_sizes.valid_block_ids()`` -- a ``FixedBlockSizeSource`` materialized at full
700	        extent), NOT a grid/M axis (not in ``fact.m_block_ids``), NOT a ROLLED reduction (absent
701	        from ``reduction_loops`` -- see below), and NOT the loop being capped itself. For
702	        ``rms_norm_per_block`` that is block 3 (``group_size``), the pinned per-group ``amax``
703	        axis resident inside the per-group quant tile; for a kernel with no such axis the product
704	        is 1 (the cap reduces to the flat ``[M_BLOCK, tile]`` form).
705	
706	        ROLLED-REDUCTION EXCLUSION: a rolled reduction axis lives in ``reduction_loops`` (its own
707	        subgraph, a SEPARATE sequential pass), NOT ``block_sizes``, so it too is non-tunable and
708	        passed the old filters -- wrongly counting it as co-resident with this loop's tile. A
709	        kernel that rolls a primary reduction over N and hand-writes an independent loop over K
710	        would then divide K's residency budget by N's full extent (e.g. 4096), crushing K's tile
711	        though N is not live during the K pass. Exclude ``reduction_loops`` axes so only genuinely
712	        co-resident pinned axes (full-extent ``FixedBlockSizeSource`` tiles, e.g. ``group_size``)
713	        bound the footprint. Byte-identical for the corpus: ``group_size`` is a fixed full-extent
714	        axis (not rolled, ``reduction_loops`` empty for the user-tiled multi-reduction kernels),
715	        so it is still counted.
716	
717	        The pinned extents live in ``env.block_sizes`` (keyed by ALL block_ids incl. non-tunable
718	        ones); with no active ``CompileEnvironment`` (a unit test exercising the block-size math
719	        on a bare ``spec``) there is nothing to enumerate, so the product defaults to 1.
720	        """
721	        from ..compile_environment import CompileEnvironment
722	        from ..compile_environment import NoCurrentEnvironment
723	
724	        try:
725	            env = CompileEnvironment.current()
726	        except NoCurrentEnvironment:
727	            return 1
728	        tunable = set(spec.block_sizes.valid_block_ids())
729	        grid = set(fact.m_block_ids)
730	        rolled = set(spec.reduction_loops.valid_block_ids())
731	        product = 1
732	        for info in env.block_sizes:
733	            bid = info.block_id
734	            # Exclude the PRIMARY reduction axis: a full-slice (materialized / pinned-grid /
735	            # rolled) primary is full-width resident and is now carried by ``r_block_resident``
736	            # in ``_build_block_sizes`` -- counting it HERE too would double-count it. (The old
737	            # code relied on a materialized primary slipping into this product to undo Defect 1's
738	            # ``r_block_resident=1`` lie; with the lie fixed, that coincidence must be removed so
739	            # the footprint stays counted exactly once.)
740	            if (
741	                bid == loop_block_id
742	                or bid == fact.primary_reduction_block_id
743	                or bid in tunable
744	                or bid in grid
745	                or bid in rolled
746	            ):
747	                continue
748	            size = info.size
749	            if isinstance(size, (int, torch.SymInt)):
750	                product *= max(1, env.size_hint(size))
751	        return product

753	    @classmethod
754	    def _m_block_cap(cls, fact: ReductionFact) -> int:
755	        """Upper bound on M_BLOCK (rows/program) for a FULL-WIDTH-output reduction, so a huge-M
756	        grid-size ``autotuner_min`` raise cannot force an occupancy-starving M_BLOCK on a
757	        memory-bound held-row reduction. A seed below ``autotuner_min`` (raised only to cap the
758	        grid) is still valid -- it survives ``normalize``.
759	
760	        The cap keeps the resident ``[M_BLOCK, rdim]`` live set inside the per-program register
761	        budget: ``M_BLOCK <= ROW_PERSIST_MAX_BYTES / (rdim * itemsize * body_live_tiles)``.
762	        Applied only via ``min`` with ``_block_floor`` (only ever LOWERS an over-raised floor)
763	        and only for full-width output -- streamed/scalar reductions ride occupancy on the
764	        chunk, not M_BLOCK, so they are uncapped.
765	        """
766	        from ..._utils import prev_power_of_2
767	
768	        if not fact.full_width_output:
769	            return (
770	                1 << 30
771	            )  # no cap: scalar/streamed occupancy rides the reduction chunk
772	        live = max(1, fact.body_live_tiles)
773	        isz = cls._resident_itemsize(fact)
774	        sh = max(1, fact.size_hint)
775	        return max(
776	            1, prev_power_of_2(max(1, cls.ROW_PERSIST_MAX_BYTES // (sh * isz * live)))
777	        )

779	    @classmethod
780	    def _m_axis_occupancy_cap(
781	        cls, env: CompileEnvironment, spec: ConfigSpec, fact: ReductionFact, mbid: int
782	    ) -> int:
783	        """Largest pow2 tile for M axis ``mbid`` that keeps the POST-widen grid at or above the
784	        occupancy floor ``num_sm * MIN_WAVES``. Widening collapses ``tile`` programs into one, so
785	        the grid is ``total_m_program_count / tile``; cap ``tile`` so that stays >= the floor.
786	
787	        JOINT across ALL tunable m-axes (Gate-T finding): when a kernel has >=2 TUNABLE grid axes
788	        (an unpinned ``hl.tile([M, P])``), ``_build_block_sizes`` widens EACH independently -- so a
789	        per-axis ``grid // floor`` cap lets the JOINT collapse (the PRODUCT of the widened tiles)
790	        blow past the floor (e.g. two axes each capped at 128 -> grid 262144 collapses to 16, 66x
791	        under floor 1056). Distribute the total collapse budget ``grid // floor`` GEOMETRICALLY
792	        across the ``n`` tunable m-axes (the ``n``-th root), so the product of the per-axis caps
793	        stays within budget. A PINNED grid axis (block_size=1, not a tunable ``block_sizes`` entry)
794	        cannot widen, so it does not consume budget and is excluded from ``n``.
795	
796	        Guards the over-collapse failure mode: a fan-out sibling whose footprint budget would
797	        permit a very wide tile must not be widened so far the GPU under-occupies. Returns 1 (NO
798	        widen) when the grid extents are not statically known: a dynamic grid has no compile-time
799	        occupancy to protect, so the conservative choice is to floor rather than risk an
800	        under-occupying widen we cannot verify.
801	        """
802	        from ..._utils import prev_power_of_2
803	        from ...runtime import get_num_sm
804	
805	        grid = _grid_rows(
806	            env, fact.m_block_ids
807	        )  # product of static m extents, 0 if dynamic
808	        if grid <= 0:
809	            return 1
810	        num_sm = max(1, get_num_sm(env.device))
811	        budget = grid // (num_sm * cls.MIN_WAVES)  # total programs we may collapse away
812	        if budget <= 1:
813	            return 1
814	        # Count the TUNABLE m-axes (the ones that can actually widen); pinned grid axes (block_size=1,
815	        # absent from spec.block_sizes) hold 1 row/program and never consume the collapse budget.
816	        tunable_ids = set(spec.block_sizes.valid_block_ids())
817	        n_tunable_m = sum(1 for b in fact.m_block_ids if b in tunable_ids)
818	        if n_tunable_m <= 1:
819	            return max(1, prev_power_of_2(max(1, budget)))
820	        # >=2 co-widening tunable m-axes: split the collapse budget geometrically so the PRODUCT of
821	        # the per-axis caps stays <= budget (the joint post-widen grid stays >= floor).
822	        per_axis = int(budget ** (1.0 / n_tunable_m))
823	        return max(1, prev_power_of_2(max(1, per_axis)))
824	
825	    @classmethod
826	    def _m_axis_block_size(cls, spec: ConfigSpec, mbid: int) -> int:
827	        """Seed block size (rows/program) for one M-axis (grid) block_id, whether or not it is
828	        a tunable ``block_sizes`` entry.
829	
830	        ``fact.m_block_ids`` is the grid axes (``tuple(sorted(grid_ids))``). A grid axis is a
831	        tunable ``block_sizes`` entry ONLY when its tile is unpinned (``hl.tile(M)``); when the
832	        user pins it (``hl.tile(M, block_size=1)``) the axis lives solely on the program grid
833	        and is absent from ``ConfigSpec.block_sizes`` (which carries only tunable tiles, indexed
834	        positionally to lay out the autotuner ``Config``). Reading the pinned axis from the
835	        tunable spec raised ``KeyError`` -- the grid-pinned-M idiom every vLLM quant kernel uses.
836	
837	        Tunable axis: its floored block size (the seed's one-row/program start, honoring a
838	        raised ``autotuner_min``). Pinned axis: its FIXED block size, read from
839	        ``env.block_sizes`` (keyed by ALL block_ids incl. grid) -- the real pinned value (1 for
840	        ``block_size=1``), never a hardcoded fallback.
841	        """
842	        if mbid in spec.block_sizes.valid_block_ids():
843	            m_idx = spec.block_sizes.block_id_to_index(mbid)
844	            return cls._block_floor(cast("BlockSizeSpec", spec.block_sizes[m_idx]))
845	        from ...runtime.config import Config as _Config
846	        from ..compile_environment import CompileEnvironment
847	
848	        env = CompileEnvironment.current()
849	        # A grid-pinned axis carries a FixedBlockSizeSource; from_config returns its pinned value
850	        # independent of the config, so an empty Config resolves it.
851	        value = env.block_sizes[mbid].from_config(_Config(block_sizes=[]))
852	        if isinstance(value, (int, torch.SymInt)):
853	            return max(1, int(value))
854	        # A non-grid-pinned axis always resolves to a static int/SymInt here (a pinned axis
855	        # carries a FixedBlockSizeSource with a concrete value), so this is a should-not-happen
856	        # fallback. Defaulting to 1 silently would reintroduce the floor-to-1 starvation the
857	        # grid-pinned handling exists to prevent -- warn loudly rather than hide it.
858	        log.warning(
859	            "reduction seed: M-axis block_id=%s resolved to a non-static block size %r; "
860	            "falling back to block_size=1 (this should not happen for a pinned grid axis)",
861	            mbid,
862	            value,
863	        )
864	        return 1

866	    @classmethod
867	    def _m_block_product(cls, spec: ConfigSpec, fact: ReductionFact) -> int:
868	        """Product of the seed's M-axis (grid) block sizes -- the number of rows each program
869	        processes (1 unless a huge-M shape raised ``autotuner_min``, capped by ``_m_block_cap``
870	        for full-width reductions). Shared by the apply-loop stream cap (``_build_block_sizes``)
871	        and the Band-C combine cap so they read the same M_BLOCK.
872	        """
873	        m_block = 1
874	        cap = cls._m_block_cap(fact)
875	        for mbid in fact.m_block_ids:
876	            m_block *= min(cls._m_axis_block_size(spec, mbid), cap)
877	        return m_block

879	    @classmethod
880	    def _build_block_sizes(
881	        cls,
882	        env: CompileEnvironment | None,
883	        spec: ConfigSpec,
884	        fact: ReductionFact,
885	        red_values: dict[int, int] | None = None,
886	        non_reduction_loop_ids: frozenset[int] | set[int] = frozenset(),
887	        grid_origin: bool = False,
888	    ) -> list[int]:
889	        """Build the ``block_sizes`` list: each reducing axis present in ``red_values`` (a
890	        ``block_id -> r_block`` map) gets its sized chunk, each non-reduction loop tile
891	        (``non_reduction_loop_ids``, disjoint from the reduction axes) gets ``loop_block``,
892	        every other axis its ``_block_floor``.
893	
894	        ``red_values`` is empty/``None`` for the STANDARD track (the reduction rides
895	        ``reduction_loops``, not a ``block_sizes`` entry) -- every axis floors. The USER-TILED
896	        track passes ``{primary_rdim: r_block}`` for a single-reduction kernel (byte-identical
897	        to the prior scalar form) and ``{axis: r_block_per_axis, ...}`` for a multi-reduction
898	        kernel (rms_norm_per_block), sizing EVERY tunable reducing axis instead of flooring the
899	        non-dominant ones to 1. A PINNED reducing axis (no tunable ``block_sizes`` slot, already
900	        full-extent resident) is simply absent from ``red_values`` -- the caller only inserts
901	        axes in ``spec.block_sizes.valid_block_ids()`` (the Error-1 guard).
902	
903	        The non-reduction loop tile matches the PRIMARY reduction tile — ``red_values[block_id]``
904	        (user-tiled) or ``next_pow2(size_hint)`` (standard, where ``red_values`` is empty). The
905	        normalize pass carries no accumulator, so this tile is a pure seed (a sane non-size-1
906	        start, never a correctness constraint); the autotuner refines it from there.
907	
908	        ``grid_origin`` (the GRID-ORIGIN M-collapse signal -- rms/ln/instance/group bwd,
909	        bias_grad/dyt) sizes each COLLAPSE-ORIGIN M (grid) axis for OCCUPANCY instead of the
910	        footprint widen below: the reduction's ORIGIN is the grid axis, reduced ACROSS programs
911	        into a per-feature accumulator, so the CTA block is occupancy-sized
912	        (``next_pow2(grid_rows // num_sm)``, capped at ``M_COLLAPSE_MAX_CTA``) to shrink the
913	        cross-CTA finalize to ~num_sm partials. It bypasses the footprint/occupancy widen caps
914	        because the grid-origin CTA block is NOT a co-resident ``[k, R_BLOCK]`` reduction tile --
915	        the resident ``[inner, feature]`` set rides a SEPARATE inner re-tile (a secondary
916	        reduction in ``red_values`` on the standard track, the primary rdim in ``red_values`` on
917	        the user-tiled track). The caller passes ``grid_origin=True`` only when that inner re-tile
918	        actually exists (``fact.grid_reduction_origin`` AND an inner-tile axis), so it is False
919	        for every non-collapse kernel and the seed stays byte-identical. Default False.
920	
921	        Occupancy-collapse is SCOPED to ``fact.grid_collapse_block_ids`` (the grid axes whose loop
922	        contains the unbacked reducing axis), NOT every ``m_block_ids`` axis: a fact can merge an
923	        independent SECOND grid loop (a plain rolled reduction), whose grid axis has no collapse
924	        origin and must floor to a grid ROW (the footprint branch below), not collapse to its full
925	        extent. Equals ``m_block_ids`` for a single-grid-loop kernel, so byte-identical there.
926	        """
927	        from ..._utils import next_power_of_2 as _np2
928	        from ..._utils import prev_power_of_2 as _pp2
929	
930	        red_values = red_values or {}
931	        # The primary (dominant) rdim value drives the normalize-loop tile; absent on the
932	        # standard track (red_values empty) where it falls back to next_pow2(size_hint).
933	        primary_red_value = red_values.get(fact.primary_reduction_block_id)
934	
935	        # Resident width of the PRIMARY reduction tile co-held when an M axis widens, used by the
936	        # footprint cap. Keyed on the FAITHFUL ACCESS signal -- is the primary a USER-TILED tunable
937	        # tile, or a FULL-SLICE resident reduction -- NOT on the contingent ``reduction_loops``
938	        # membership (Defect 1: that key flips with whether ANOTHER reduction shares the loop, since
939	        # the roller rolls at most one per loop; a materialized full-slice reduction that lost the
940	        # one roll-slot is full-width resident yet the old ``else`` branch told it ``1`` -- a lie).
941	        #   - USER-TILED (rdim is a tunable ``block_sizes`` entry, in ``red_values``): resident at
942	        #     its sized r_block (already capped, e.g. kl_div's carried-tile-capped 4096).
943	        #   - FULL-SLICE (everything else -- ROLLED into ``reduction_loops``, MATERIALIZED full-width
944	        #     the roller declined, or a PINNED full-extent grid axis): the whole extent is resident,
945	        #     so the faithful width is ``next_pow2(size_hint)``. This ONE branch unifies the three
946	        #     contingent routes the old code split (rolled / else=1 / else=1) onto the access fact.
947	        # Counted EXACTLY ONCE: ``_pinned_inner_resident_elems`` now EXCLUDES the primary reduction
948	        # axis (it is always carried here), so a full-slice primary is no longer double-counted by
949	        # the inner product (the old code relied on the materialized primary slipping INTO that
950	        # product to undo the ``else=1`` lie -- a two-wrongs-cancel coincidence now removed).
951	        if primary_red_value is not None:
952	            r_block_resident = primary_red_value
953	        else:
954	            r_block_resident = _np2(fact.size_hint)
955	
956	        loop_block: int | None = None
957	        if non_reduction_loop_ids:
958	            # The apply/normalize tile starts at the reduction tile — primary red_value
959	            # (user-tiled) or next_pow2(size_hint) (standard, where red_values is empty)...
960	            loop_block = (
961	                primary_red_value
962	                if primary_red_value is not None
963	                else _np2(fact.size_hint)
964	            )
965	            # ...then is clamped to the same M_BLOCK-aware footprint cap as the reduction
966	            # tile (the apply tile is [M_BLOCK, loop_block] resident, so a wide one spills).
967	            # Only the Band-C reduce-then-apply kernels (welford, groupnorm) have a normalize
968	            # loop, so everything else is byte-identical (no non_reduction_loop_ids). The cap
969	            # clamps an otherwise-spilling apply pass back to register residency; the pass is
970	            # memory-bound so this is a net win. A flat per-row cap always narrowed it.
971	            loop_block = min(loop_block, cls._resident_tile_cap(spec, fact))
972	
973	        out: list[int] = []
974	        for i in range(len(spec.block_sizes)):
975	            bs_spec = cast("BlockSizeSpec", spec.block_sizes[i])
976	            if bs_spec.block_id in red_values:
977	                # ANY reducing axis with a tunable slot (the primary rdim, or a secondary
978	                # reducing axis in a multi-reduction kernel) -- size it to its own r_block.
979	                out.append(red_values[bs_spec.block_id])
980	            elif bs_spec.block_id in non_reduction_loop_ids and loop_block is not None:
981	                out.append(loop_block)
982	            elif bs_spec.block_id in fact.grid_collapse_block_ids and grid_origin:
983	                # GRID-ORIGIN M-collapse (rms/ln/instance/group bwd, bias_grad/dyt): occupancy-size
984	                # this tunable M (grid) axis (see the ``grid_origin`` docstring above). Bypasses the
985	                # footprint/occupancy widen caps below -- the CTA block is NOT a co-resident
986	                # ``[k, R_BLOCK]`` reduction tile (the resident set rides a separate inner re-tile).
987	                # Needs a live ``env`` (every grid-origin seed has one); the cap is a no-op for the
988	                # corpus (all collapse grid blocks <= 64 << M_COLLAPSE_MAX_CTA).
989	                #
990	                # Scoped to ``grid_collapse_block_ids`` (the collapse-origin loop's grid axes), NOT
991	                # every ``m_block_ids`` axis: one fact can merge several independent top-level grid
992	                # loops, but only the loop holding the unbacked reducing axis is the collapse origin.
993	                # A grid axis from ANOTHER loop (a plain rolled reduction fused into the same fact)
994	                # falls through to the footprint branch below and floors to a grid ROW -- it has no
995	                # collapse origin, so occupancy-collapsing it to full extent would starve the grid.
996	                # For a single-grid-loop kernel ``grid_collapse_block_ids == m_block_ids``, so this
997	                # is byte-identical for every corpus M-collapse kernel.
998	                m_cta = cls._m_collapse_grid_block(
999	                    cast("CompileEnvironment", env), fact, cap=cls.M_COLLAPSE_MAX_CTA
1000	                )
1001	                out.append(m_cta)
1002	            elif bs_spec.block_id in fact.m_block_ids:
1003	                # Size this tunable grid (M) axis by the FOOTPRINT it would produce, not by any
1004	                # row-vs-sibling classification. Widening this axis by ``k`` holds a
1005	                # ``[k, R_BLOCK]`` resident reduction tile, so ``_resident_tile_cap`` (now keyed on
1006	                # the resident R_BLOCK) is the largest ``k`` that fits the register budget. The
1007	                # floor-vs-widen outcome falls out of the arithmetic:
1008	                #   - a LARGE-R_BLOCK reduction (rms_norm, R_BLOCK=16384) -> cap ~= 1-2 (widening
1009	                #     would spill), so the axis effectively FLOORS, capped further by _m_block_cap;
1010	                #   - a TINY-R_BLOCK reduction (per_token_group / a full-slice per-group amax,
1011	                #     R_BLOCK=128) -> cap is large, so a fan-out sibling WIDENS (the per_token_group
1012	                #     2x win, and the full-slice variant fix) -- regardless of how the kernel is
1013	                #     written (grid-pinned, specialized, or rolled-full-extent).
1014	                # Occupancy guard: never widen so far the POST-widen grid drops below
1015	                # ``num_sm * MIN_WAVES`` (collapsing too many programs would under-occupy).
1016	                inner = cls._pinned_inner_resident_elems(spec, fact, bs_spec.block_id)
1017	                fits = cls._resident_tile_cap(
1018	                    spec, fact, inner, r_block_resident=r_block_resident
1019	                )
1020	                # A carried-2D-tile reduction (Band B: kl_div/jsd) holds an [M_BLOCK, R_BLOCK]
1021	                # accumulator LIVE across the whole loop, so widening M_BLOCK by k multiplies that
1022	                # carried tile by k against the tight CARRIED_TILE_MAX_BYTES budget. Cap the widen
1023	                # by that footprint too -- the SHARED _carried_tile_budget (co_resident=R_BLOCK),
1024	                # rounded DOWN (largest k that fits).
1025	                if fact.num_carried_2d_tiles >= 1:
1026	                    carried = cls._carried_tile_budget(
1027	                        fact, co_resident=r_block_resident
1028	                    )
1029	                    fits = min(fits, _pp2(max(1, carried)))
1030	                own = _np2(bs_spec.size_hint)
1031	                # Occupancy cap needs a device (env) to know the grid/SM count; without one (a
1032	                # bare-spec unit test, or any context with no live env) we cannot verify the
1033	                # post-widen grid stays saturated, so floor conservatively (occ=1) -- never widen
1034	                # a value we cannot occupancy-check. Mirrors the dynamic-grid default.
1035	                occ = (
1036	                    cls._m_axis_occupancy_cap(env, spec, fact, bs_spec.block_id)
1037	                    if env is not None
1038	                    else 1
1039	                )
1040	                floor = cls._block_floor(bs_spec)
1041	                # Widen to the largest pow2 that (a) fits the resident-footprint budget, (b) keeps
1042	                # the post-widen grid above the occupancy floor, and (c) does not exceed the axis
1043	                # extent; never below the per-axis floor, never above the M_BLOCK register cap.
1044	                widened = max(floor, min(own, fits, occ, cls._m_block_cap(fact)))
1045	                out.append(widened)
1046	            else:
1047	                # An INDEPENDENT non-grid tunable loop: by elimination, not a reducing axis
1048	                # (not in ``red_values``), not an extent-matching apply/normalize loop (not in
1049	                # ``non_reduction_loop_ids``), and not the grid-M axis (not in ``m_block_ids``,
1050	                # which has its own branch above). The ONLY remaining shape is a standalone
1051	                # tiled loop at its own extent -- ``rms_norm_per_block``'s ``groups_per_row``
1052	                # pass is the canonical case. Flooring it to 1 serialized that pass (the
1053	                # [..., 1] catastrophe); widen to its own extent (read from the passed-in
1054	                # ``bs_spec``, never the global env), capped by the SAME resident-byte budget as
1055	                # the apply/normalize tile so a huge loop cannot spill. Flooring was only ever
1056	                # the right default to catch the grid axis, which is now handled above -- so
1057	                # widening, not ``_block_floor``, is the principled catch-all. NO existing
1058	                # reduction kernel reaches this branch (their only non-reducing/non-apply axis
1059	                # IS the grid-M axis), so it is a no-op for the 23-kernel corpus and changes
1060	                # only the new block-quant kernels. The cap divides the budget by the PINNED
1061	                # inner axes co-resident in this loop's tile (rms_norm_per_block: ``group_size``),
1062	                # so the ``[M_BLOCK, loop_tile, *pinned_inner]`` footprint is bounded faithfully
1063	                # -- a flat ``[M_BLOCK, tile]`` cap would under-count and admit a spilling tile.
1064	                inner = cls._pinned_inner_resident_elems(spec, fact, bs_spec.block_id)
1065	                own = _np2(bs_spec.size_hint)
1066	                out.append(max(1, min(own, cls._resident_tile_cap(spec, fact, inner))))
1067	        return out

1069	    @classmethod
1070	    def _eviction_policies(
1071	        cls,
1072	        env: CompileEnvironment,
1073	        kind: str,
1074	        reread_slot: int | None = None,
1075	    ) -> list[str] | None:
1076	        """``load_eviction_policies`` list (spec length), keyed on per-load residency;
1077	        None leaves the autotuner default.
1078	
1079	        - ``"stream"`` — single streamed input (``num_load == 1``: sum, long_sum), read
1080	          once: every load -> ``'first'`` (frees L2).
1081	        - ``"reread"`` — the row is re-read across passes: its first load -> ``'last'``
1082	          (L2-resident), rest -> ``'first'``. ``reread_slot`` is that load's actual slot,
1083	          read directly from ``ReductionFact.reread_eviction_index`` (the re-read load's
1084	          ``MemoryOpFact.eviction_index``), not guessed or re-walked per config.
1085	
1086	        Other kinds leave the default until a per-slot win is confirmed.
1087	        """
1088	        n = env.config_spec.load_eviction_policies.length
1089	        if n <= 0:
1090	            return None
1091	        if kind == "stream":
1092	            return ["first"] * n
1093	        if kind == "reread":
1094	            if reread_slot is None or not 0 <= reread_slot < n:
1095	                return None
1096	            policy = ["first"] * n
1097	            policy[reread_slot] = "last"
1098	            return policy
1099	        return None

1101	    @classmethod
1102	    def _reduction_rblock(
1103	        cls,
1104	        env: CompileEnvironment,
1105	        fact: ReductionFact,
1106	        m_block: int,
1107	        footprint_factor: int = 1,
1108	        rnumel: int | None = None,
1109	    ) -> tuple[int, bool]:
1110	        """The reduction-axis chunk (pow2) AND the persistent verdict, decided together in one
1111	        budgeted formula and shared by both tracks. Returns ``(r_block, persistent)``.
1112	
1113	        ``rnumel`` is the reduction-axis extent to size against; it defaults to
1114	        ``fact.size_hint`` (the PRIMARY rdim) so single-reduction callers are unchanged. A
1115	        multi-reduction kernel (``rms_norm_per_block``-class) calls this once per TUNABLE
1116	        secondary reducing axis in ``fact.secondary_reduction_block_ids``, passing that axis's own
1117	        ``env.block_sizes[b].size_hint()`` so each axis is chunked against its OWN extent (the
1118	        passes are sequential / not co-resident, so a secondary axis is sized independently --
1119	        see the per-axis ``red_values`` construction in each ``get_seed_config``).
1120	
1121	        ``footprint_factor`` = how many resident rdim-shaped tiles one program holds live at
1122	        the peak (1 = a single result tile). It bounds the decision two ways:
1123	        - PERSISTENT additionally requires (besides ``row_reread`` and no carried 2-D tile) the
1124	          single resident tile to fit ``ROW_PERSIST_MAX_BYTES`` AND the full
1125	          ``footprint_factor``-tile resident set to fit ``LIVE_PERSIST_BUDGET`` (the multi-tile
1126	          spill ceiling). This liveness term only ever REMOVES persistence from a heavy body.
1127	        - the LOOPED chunk is shrunk by ``footprint_factor`` so a heavy body gets a smaller
1128	          chunk, keeping the looped resident set inside the register budget.
1129	
1130	        The standard track passes ``footprint_factor=body_live_tiles``; the user-tiled track
1131	        keeps the default ``1`` (where ``LIVE_PERSIST_BUDGET`` collapses to the base byte cap,
1132	        a no-op). The carried-2-D-tile cap (kl_div/jsd) is folded into the chunk decision.
1133	
1134	        No welford "structured-combine floor": register-residency via the footprint cap is what
1135	        matters; welford is memory-bound and a wide combine tile only spills.
1136	        """
1137	        from ..._utils import next_power_of_2 as _np2
1138	        from ..._utils import prev_power_of_2
1139	
1140	        # extent: the axis being sized. Defaults to the primary rdim (fact.size_hint) so every
1141	        # single-reduction caller is byte-identical; a multi-reduction caller passes a secondary
1142	        # axis's own extent.
1143	        extent = fact.size_hint if rnumel is None else rnumel
1144	        rdim = _np2(extent)
1145	        # The persist/loop byte caps bound the RESIDENT fp32-accumulator tile, not the bf16/fp16
1146	        # input row, so floor the width at fp32 (max(itemsize,4)) -- else a half-precision row
1147	        # is told it fits persistent when its fp32 reduction tile would spill (the bf16
1148	        # saturation-check finding: N=65536 bf16 wrongly persists, fp32 accumulator = 256 KiB).
1149	        itemsize = cls._resident_itemsize(fact)
1150	        m = max(1, m_block)
1151	        ff = max(1, footprint_factor)
1152	        # Persistent iff (a) a SINGLE result tile fits the per-program caps (the element compile
1153	        # limit element_cap AND the ROW_PERSIST_MAX_BYTES single-tile byte cap), AND (b) the full
1154	        # ff-tile resident set fits LIVE_PERSIST_BUDGET. (b) is the liveness ceiling: it only
1155	        # removes persistence from a heavy body, never grants it (no-op at ff==1).
1156	        element_cap = env.backend.max_tensor_numel
1157	        # Hold the full extent one-shot iff it clears every per-program ceiling (element compile
1158	        # limit element_cap, ROW_PERSIST_MAX_BYTES byte cap, LIVE_PERSIST_BUDGET live-set cap) AND
1159	        # there is NO carried 2-D accumulator -- a [M_BLOCK, R_BLOCK] tile carried across the loop
1160	        # is too heavy to hold, so stream.
1161	        extent_held = (
1162	            # Persist captures a re-read prize iff looping would RE-READ the row: a full-width apply
1163	            # (rms/layer_norm/softmax/welford) or a second reduction needing the first's result
1164	            # (cross_entropy's logsumexp -- which full_width_output misses). row_reread catches both;
1165	            # num_carried_2d_tiles == 0 keeps kl_div/jsd off persist (they re-read regardless).
1166	            fact.row_reread
1167	            and fact.num_carried_2d_tiles == 0
1168	            and (element_cap is None or extent <= element_cap)
1169	            and (m * extent * itemsize <= cls.ROW_PERSIST_MAX_BYTES)
1170	            and (ff * m * extent * itemsize <= cls.LIVE_PERSIST_BUDGET)
1171	        )
1172	        if extent_held:
1173	            r_block = rdim
1174	        else:
1175	            # Can't hold the extent -> stream it at the occupancy-optimal LOOPED_CHUNK (M_BLOCK- and
1176	            # liveness-shrunk); a capacity-sized chunk would re-read AND lower occupancy.
1177	            budget = cls.ROW_PERSIST_MAX_BYTES // (m * itemsize * ff)
1178	            r_block = min(cls.LOOPED_CHUNK, prev_power_of_2(budget))
1179	            # Carried 2-D accumulators (kl_div, jsd) always reach this branch; cap R_BLOCK by its tighter
1180	            # byte budget to avoid catastrophic register spills. No-op when num_carried_2d_tiles == 0.
1181	            if fact.num_carried_2d_tiles >= 1:
1182	                r_block = min(r_block, cls._carried_tile_r_block_cap(fact))
1183	        # Never size the chunk past the (padded) extent: clamp to rdim so a sub-cap-N carried reduction
1184	        # matches the old held branch and keeps `persistent` below correct.
1185	        r_block = max(1, min(r_block, rdim))
1186	        # `persistent` is READ OFF the final chunk -- held iff the chunk reached the extent
1187	        # (reduction_loops=[None] standard, or R_BLOCK == rdim user-tiled), never set separately.
1188	        return r_block, r_block >= rdim

1191	    def _m_collapse_grid_block(
1192	        cls, env: CompileEnvironment, fact: ReductionFact, cap: int | None = None
1193	    ) -> int:
1194	        """Occupancy-sized grid M block for a grad-parameter M-collapse (rms/ln/instance/group
1195	        backward on the standard track; bias_grad/dyt on the user-tiled track). The
1196	        grad-parameter (``grad_weight[N]`` / ``grad_bias[N]``) is summed across the grid rows
1197	        into a per-CTA partial finalized by a cross-CTA ``sum(0)``; with the block floored to 1
1198	        that is a grid-wide M-way collapse (one partial/row), so size it to ~one SM wave
1199	        (``next_pow2(grid_rows // num_sm)``) to cut it to ~``num_sm`` partials.
1200	
1201	        The grid-rows numerator is the product over the COLLAPSE-ORIGIN grid axes
1202	        (``grid_collapse_block_ids``), the loop actually being collapsed -- NOT the conflated
1203	        product over every ``m_block_ids`` axis (which can span an unrelated SECOND grid loop whose
1204	        rows belong to a different launch, inflating the occupancy numerator). It equals
1205	        ``m_block_ids`` for a single-grid-loop kernel, so byte-identical for the corpus.
1206	
1207	        ``cap`` bounds the block when it ALSO bears the reduction slab (user-tiled pure
1208	        collapse, capped at ``M_COLLAPSE_MAX_CTA``); the standard track leaves it uncapped
1209	        because the resident ``[inner, feature]`` set rides a separate inner re-tile, not this
1210	        block. A dynamic/unbacked grid (``grid_rows == 0``) collapses to 1.
1211	        """
1212	        from ..._utils import next_power_of_2 as _np2
1213	        from ...runtime import get_num_sm
1214	
1215	        grid_rows = _grid_rows(env, fact.grid_collapse_block_ids)
1216	        num_sm = max(1, get_num_sm(env.device))
1217	        block = _np2(max(1, grid_rows // num_sm))
1218	        return max(1, block if cap is None else min(cap, block))

1220	    @classmethod
1221	    def _m_collapse_inner_byte_cap(cls, feat_bytes: int) -> int:
1222	        """Largest pow2 inner reduction tile whose resident ``[inner, feature]`` fp32 set fits
1223	        ``M_COLLAPSE_TILE_BYTES``, given the per-row feature footprint ``feat_bytes``. Both
1224	        M-collapse tracks pass ``fact.feature_footprint * itemsize`` (the PRODUCT of the
1225	        materialized feature axes); for a 2-D norm that product is the single feature axis.
1226	        """
1227	        from ..._utils import next_power_of_2 as _np2
1228	
1229	        return max(1, _np2(max(1, cls.M_COLLAPSE_TILE_BYTES // max(1, feat_bytes))))

from __future__ import annotations

import functools
import json
import logging
from pathlib import Path
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
from typing import Any
from typing import cast

import torch

from ...autotuner.config_fragment import EnumFragment
from ...runtime.config import Config
from .common import REDUCTION_TARGET_NAMES
from .common import clamp_block_size_targets
from .common import matches_hardware
from .common import op_name_parts
from .registry import AutotunerHeuristic

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from ...autotuner.config_spec import BlockSizeSpec
    from ...autotuner.config_spec import ConfigSpec
    from ...autotuner.config_spec import MatmulFact
    from ...autotuner.config_spec import ReductionFact
    from ..compile_environment import CompileEnvironment
    from ..device_ir import DeviceIR


log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

_B200_MATMUL_HEURISTICS_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "matmul_b200.json"


# Heuristic was originally contributed by @umechand-amd
# in https://github.com/pytorch/helion/pull/2357.
class TritonSkinnyGemmHeuristic(AutotunerHeuristic):
    name = "triton_skinny_gemm"
    backend = "triton"
    MIN_ASPECT_RATIO = 8
    BLOCK_TARGETS = (64, 64, 256)
    HARDWARE_TARGETS = (("cuda", "sm90"), ("rocm", "gfx950"))

    @classmethod
    def is_eligible(cls, env: CompileEnvironment, device_ir: DeviceIR) -> bool:
        if not matches_hardware(env, cls.HARDWARE_TARGETS):
            return False
        facts = env.config_spec.matmul_facts
        if len(facts) != 1:
            return False
        fact = facts[0]
        if fact.lhs_ndim != 2 or fact.rhs_ndim != 2:
            return False
        if (
            fact.static_m is None
            or fact.static_n is None
            or fact.static_k is None
            or fact.m_block_id is None
            or fact.n_block_id is None
            or fact.k_block_id is None
        ):
            return False
        if max(fact.static_m, fact.static_n) < cls.MIN_ASPECT_RATIO * min(
            fact.static_m, fact.static_n
        ):
            return False
        return (
            clamp_block_size_targets(
                env,
                [
                    (fact.m_block_id, fact.static_m, cls.BLOCK_TARGETS[0]),
                    (fact.n_block_id, fact.static_n, cls.BLOCK_TARGETS[1]),
                    (fact.k_block_id, fact.static_k, cls.BLOCK_TARGETS[2]),
                ],
            )
            is not None
        )

    @classmethod
    def get_seed_config(cls, env: CompileEnvironment, device_ir: DeviceIR) -> Config:
        assert len(env.config_spec.matmul_facts) == 1
        fact = env.config_spec.matmul_facts[0]
        assert fact.static_m is not None
        assert fact.static_n is not None
        assert fact.static_k is not None
        assert fact.m_block_id is not None
        assert fact.n_block_id is not None
        assert fact.k_block_id is not None
        block_sizes = clamp_block_size_targets(
            env,
            [
                (fact.m_block_id, fact.static_m, cls.BLOCK_TARGETS[0]),
                (fact.n_block_id, fact.static_n, cls.BLOCK_TARGETS[1]),
                (fact.k_block_id, fact.static_k, cls.BLOCK_TARGETS[2]),
            ],
        )
        assert block_sizes is not None
        return Config(block_sizes=block_sizes)


def _dtype_family_from_dtype(dtype: object) -> str:
    dtype = str(dtype)
    if "float16" in dtype or "bfloat16" in dtype:
        return "fp16_bf16"
    if "float32" in dtype:
        return "fp32"
    return "other"


def _single_2d_static_matmul_fact(config_spec: ConfigSpec) -> MatmulFact | None:
    facts = config_spec.matmul_facts
    if len(facts) != 1 or len(config_spec.block_sizes) != 3:
        return None
    fact = facts[0]
    if fact.lhs_ndim != 2 or fact.rhs_ndim != 2:
        return None
    if fact.static_m is None or fact.static_n is None or fact.static_k is None:
        return None
    if (fact.m_block_id, fact.n_block_id, fact.k_block_id) != (0, 1, 2):
        return None
    return fact


def _shape_bucket_from_fact(fact: MatmulFact) -> dict[str, object]:
    assert fact.static_m is not None
    assert fact.static_n is not None
    assert fact.static_k is not None
    return {
        "dtype": _dtype_family_from_dtype(fact.lhs_dtype),
        "m_value": fact.static_m,
        "n_value": fact.static_n,
        "k_value": fact.static_k,
    }


@functools.cache
def _heuristic_rules() -> tuple[dict[str, object], ...]:
    with _B200_MATMUL_HEURISTICS_PATH.open(encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        data = cast("dict[str, list[dict[str, object]]]", json.load(handle))
    return tuple(data["rules"])


def _interval_contains(interval: str, value: int) -> bool:
    lower_text, upper_text = interval[1:-1].split(",", maxsplit=1)
    lower = float(lower_text)
    upper = float("inf") if upper_text == "inf" else float(upper_text)

    lower_ok = value >= lower if interval[0] == "[" else value > lower
    upper_ok = value <= upper if interval[-1] == "]" else value < upper
    return lower_ok and upper_ok


def _shape_bucket_matches(
    rule_bucket: dict[str, object],
    query_bucket: dict[str, object],
) -> bool:
    for key, value in rule_bucket.items():
        if key in {"k_bucket", "m_bucket", "n_bucket"}:
            intervals = value if isinstance(value, list) else [value]
            dim_value = cast("int", query_bucket[f"{key[0]}_value"])
            if not any(
                _interval_contains(cast("str", interval), dim_value)
                for interval in intervals
            ):
                return False
            continue
        query_value = query_bucket.get(key)
        values = value if isinstance(value, list) else [value]
        if query_value not in values:
            return False
    return True


def _rules_for_bucket(
    shape_bucket: dict[str, object],
) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
    matches = [
        rule
        for rule in _heuristic_rules()
        if _shape_bucket_matches(
            cast("dict[str, object]", rule["shape_bucket"]),
            shape_bucket,
        )
    ]
    matches.sort(
        key=lambda rule: len(cast("dict[str, object]", rule["shape_bucket"])),
        reverse=True,
    )
    return matches


def _materialize_config(
    raw: dict[str, object],
    *,
    config_spec: ConfigSpec,
) -> Config:
    flat_fields = config_spec._flat_fields()
    supported = {key: value for key, value in raw.items() if key in flat_fields}
    allowed_pid_types = config_spec.allowed_pid_types
    if (
        "pid_type" in supported
        and allowed_pid_types
        and supported["pid_type"] not in allowed_pid_types
    ):
        supported.pop("pid_type")
    config_spec.normalize(supported, _fix_invalid=True)
    config = Config(**cast("dict[str, Any]", supported))
    config_spec._shrink_for_numel_constraints(config)
    return config


def _seed_config_for_bucket(
    shape_bucket: dict[str, object],
    *,
    config_spec: ConfigSpec,
) -> Config | None:
    rules = _rules_for_bucket(shape_bucket)
    if not rules:
        return None

    for rule in rules:
        for template in cast("list[dict[str, object]]", rule["templates"]):
            return _materialize_config(template, config_spec=config_spec)
    return None


def _seed_config_for_config_spec(config_spec: ConfigSpec) -> Config | None:
    fact = _single_2d_static_matmul_fact(config_spec)
    if fact is None:
        return None
    return _seed_config_for_bucket(
        _shape_bucket_from_fact(fact),
        config_spec=config_spec,
    )


class TritonB200MatmulHeuristic(AutotunerHeuristic):
    name = "triton_b200_matmul"
    backend = "triton"
    promote_seed_to_default = True
    HARDWARE_TARGETS = (("cuda", "sm100"),)

    @classmethod
    def is_eligible(
        cls,
        env: CompileEnvironment,
        device_ir: DeviceIR,
    ) -> bool:
        return matches_hardware(env, cls.HARDWARE_TARGETS)

    @classmethod
    def get_seed_config(
        cls,
        env: CompileEnvironment,
        device_ir: DeviceIR,
    ) -> Config | None:
        return _seed_config_for_config_spec(env.config_spec)


class TritonSplitJoinRotateHeuristic(AutotunerHeuristic):
    """Seed all-ones ``block_sizes`` for split/join rotate kernels (rope).

    These kernels load a large untiled inner slab per program, so tiling any
    outer dim past 1 only wastes work and overflows Triton's block-numel cap.
    Detected by ``hl.split`` + ``hl.join`` with no matmul and no reduction op.
    """

    name = "triton_split_join_rotate"
    backend = "triton"

    @classmethod
    def is_eligible(cls, env: CompileEnvironment, device_ir: DeviceIR) -> bool:
        # A GEMM (even fused) is not a rope-style rotate.
        if env.config_spec.matmul_facts:
            return False
        if not env.config_spec.block_sizes:
            return False
        # Local import avoids a circular import at module load
        # (runtime.kernel -> autotuner_heuristics -> helion.language).
        from ...language import join as hl_join
        from ...language import split as hl_split

        saw_split = False
        saw_join = False
        for graph_info in device_ir.graphs:
            for node in graph_info.graph.nodes:
                if node.op != "call_function":
                    continue
                target = node.target
                if target is hl_split:
                    saw_split = True
                elif target is hl_join:
                    saw_join = True
                elif op_name_parts(target) & REDUCTION_TARGET_NAMES:
                    # Fused reduction → not a pure rotate; keep its own tiling.
                    return False
        return saw_split and saw_join

    @classmethod
    def get_seed_config(cls, env: CompileEnvironment, device_ir: DeviceIR) -> Config:
        return Config(block_sizes=[1] * len(env.config_spec.block_sizes))


class TritonPointwiseSeedHeuristic(AutotunerHeuristic):
    """Seed a bandwidth-saturating tile for PURE elementwise/pointwise kernels.

    A pointwise kernel reads its inputs, computes, and writes its outputs with no
    reduction / matmul / loop-carried accumulator — it is BANDWIDTH-bound. The compiler
    default tiles it at ``block_size=32`` (``BlockSizeSpec._fragment``: ``total_ndim <= 2
    and reduction_numel <= 128``), moving only ~10% of HBM (~5-7x slower than a saturating
    tile; measured headroom in ``_lab/pointwise``). This seed sizes the tile to (a) a byte
    budget that saturates HBM and (b) the grid occupancy (size_hint-aware), keyed on the
    derived ``PointwiseElementwiseFact`` (bytes/elem + total numel) — NEVER on the
    activation identity or a dtype literal. Fires on the presence of that fact, which is
    built only on the ABSENCE of the reduction/matmul/accumulator facts (disjointness rule),
    so it never claws a reducing kernel into the pointwise track.
    """

    name = "triton_pointwise"
    backend = "triton"

    # Hill-climbed constants (see _lab/pointwise/NOTEBOOK.md). TILE_BYTES=8192 gives a ~1024-elem
    # tile for traffic-3 (swiglu/geglu/residual_add) and ~2048 for traffic-2 (relu²/bias_gelu) —
    # the robust zone: 1-D kernels are flat across 1-8K, but N-D/traffic-2 kernels (bias_gelu) lose
    # ~5-25% at 4096 vs 2048, so the smaller budget lifts the worst kernel with no 1-D regression.
    TILE_BYTES = 8192  # target HBM bytes moved per tile
    MIN_WAVES = 8  # grid >= num_sm * MIN_WAVES (size_hint-aware grid floor)
    BLOCK_FLOOR = 256  # never regress toward the bs=32 default

    @classmethod
    def is_eligible(cls, env: CompileEnvironment, device_ir: DeviceIR) -> bool:
        return bool(env.config_spec.pointwise_facts)

    @classmethod
    def get_seed_config(cls, env: CompileEnvironment, device_ir: DeviceIR) -> Config:
        from ...runtime import get_num_sm
        from ...runtime.config import Config as _Config

        spec = env.config_spec
        fact = spec.pointwise_facts[0]
        num_sm = max(1, get_num_sm(env.device))
        bytes_per_elem = max(1, fact.bytes_per_elem)
        # PINNED per-program elements: a grid-pinned (block_size=1) or specialized full-extent
        # axis contributes elements to EVERY program but has no tunable tile, so the distributor
        # (which only sees spec.block_sizes) cannot account for them. Their product is the work
        # each program already does; the tunable dims only need to fill the REMAINING budget.
        # (A grid-pinned block_size=1 axis contributes 1 -> no effect; a specialized group_size
        # contributes its full width.) Read the fixed block size from env.block_sizes (keyed by
        # ALL ids) via an empty Config, NOT size_hint (which is the whole-axis extent, not the
        # per-program tile).
        tunable = set(spec.block_sizes.valid_block_ids())
        pinned_elems = 1
        for info in env.block_sizes:
            if info.block_id in tunable:
                continue
            value = info.from_config(_Config(block_sizes=[]))
            if isinstance(value, (int, torch.SymInt)):
                pinned_elems *= max(1, int(value))
        # Bytes-aware target tile (in elements), DISCOUNTED by the pinned per-program work: a
        # traffic-3 kernel moves 50% more bytes per element than traffic-2, so for the same byte
        # budget it gets a SMALLER element tile.
        target = max(1, (cls.TILE_BYTES // bytes_per_elem) // pinned_elems)
        # size_hint-aware: cap the tile so the grid keeps the SMs busy on small problems (the
        # occupancy cap already uses the pinned-inclusive total_numel, so divide it too).
        max_tile = max(1, fact.total_numel // (num_sm * cls.MIN_WAVES) // pinned_elems)
        target = max(1, min(target, max_tile))
        # Floor (the never-regress-to-bs=32 guard) likewise discounts the pinned work: a program
        # already covering >= BLOCK_FLOOR elements via pinned axes needs no tunable floor.
        floor = max(1, cls.BLOCK_FLOOR // pinned_elems)
        target = max(floor, target)
        # block_sizes is the only non-default field; num_warps/num_stages/pid_type stay at the
        # compiler defaults (4 / 1 / 'flat'), so emitting them would be inert (Gate F). A measured
        # num_warps ramp for large tiles is a BROADEN-queue item.
        return Config(block_sizes=cls._seed_block_sizes(spec, target, floor))

    @staticmethod
    def _pow2_floor(value: int) -> int:
        return 1 << (value.bit_length() - 1) if value >= 1 else 1

    @classmethod
    def _clamp_dim(cls, target: int, bs_spec: BlockSizeSpec, floor: int) -> int:
        # Round DOWN to a pow2 within [floor (and the spec's correctness min), max_size]. max_size
        # is next_pow2(extent), so capping there (rather than pre-capping at the raw size_hint) lets
        # the inner tile COVER a short row in one masked tile (extent 768 -> 1024, not floored to
        # 512). autotuner_min is the AUTOTUNER's search floor, NOT a seed constraint (the reduction
        # and split-join seeds emit block=1 below it), so it is intentionally not applied here.
        cand = cls._pow2_floor(max(1, target))
        cand = max(cand, floor, bs_spec.min_size)
        cand = min(cand, bs_spec.max_size)
        return max(1, cand)

    @classmethod
    def _seed_block_sizes(
        cls, spec: ConfigSpec, target: int, floor: int | None = None
    ) -> list[int]:
        """Distribute the target tile (in elements) across the block dims, INNERMOST first,
        SPILLING the leftover budget outward. The innermost (contiguous, last) dim takes as much
        of the budget as its extent allows (capped at max_size = next_pow2(extent), so a short row
        is covered in one masked tile); whatever budget it cannot absorb spills to the next-outer
        dim, and so on. Because a row-major tensor stores rows contiguously, an ``[R, N]`` tile of
        a short-N tensor is still a coalesced ``R*N`` contiguous block — so a tall-skinny tensor
        (small inner extent, e.g. image RGBA N=4 or a per-head N=64) gets a budget-sized tile (e.g.
        ``[128, 8]``) instead of a starved ``[1, 8]`` that regresses below the bs=32 default. For a
        WIDE row (extent >= budget) the inner absorbs the whole budget and the outer dims stay 1
        (``[1, 1024]``) — the 1-D-flatten-equivalent coalesced run; for a 1-D kernel this is just
        ``[clamp(target)]``."""
        inner_floor = cls.BLOCK_FLOOR if floor is None else floor
        n = len(spec.block_sizes)
        specs = [cast("BlockSizeSpec", spec.block_sizes[i]) for i in range(n)]
        block = [1] * n
        remaining = max(1, target)
        for i in reversed(
            range(n)
        ):  # innermost (contiguous) dim first, spill the rest outward
            dim_floor = inner_floor if i == n - 1 else 1
            block[i] = cls._clamp_dim(remaining, specs[i], dim_floor)
            remaining = max(1, remaining // block[i])
            if remaining <= 1:
                break
        return block


def _triton_reduction_eligible(env: CompileEnvironment, device_ir: DeviceIR) -> bool:
    """Gate: at least one ``ReductionFact`` and no ``matmul_facts``. Admits both tracks
    (standard rollable, user-tiled); excludes GEMMs.

    FIRES on a MULTI-FACT kernel too (two genuinely-independent reductions in separate loops,
    e.g. ``out1 = x.sum(-1); out2 = y.sum(-1)`` -> two ``ReductionFact``s). The old ``== 1`` gate
    declined those into the (bad) upstream default -- an under-firing FENCE narrowing to the
    single-reduction curriculum (no corpus kernel has >1 fact). A seed is never forced (a worse
    seed only costs autotuning time, never correctness), so FIRING a best-guess on the dominant
    (max-extent) reduction beats declining into the default (method §2 'prefer to fire'); the
    seeded loop is sized correctly and the other loop's tiles ride the generic per-axis path.
    ``_reduction_primary_fact`` picks the dominant fact for the seed."""
    spec = env.config_spec
    return len(spec.reduction_facts) >= 1 and not spec.matmul_facts


def _reduction_primary_fact(spec: ConfigSpec) -> ReductionFact:
    """The fact the seed sizes when a kernel has MORE THAN ONE ReductionFact (independent
    reductions in separate loops): the DOMINANT one by reduction extent (``size_hint``), the
    same max-extent tie-break the single-fact dominant-axis pick uses. The single-fact case
    returns ``reduction_facts[0]`` unchanged (byte-identical). A worse pick only costs autotune
    time (the other loop's tiles are still sized by ``_build_block_sizes``); the dominant
